stemMd: A student solves $5(2x-3)=3x+20$. The student correctly writes $10x-15=3x+20$, but then incorrectly writes $7x=5$. Which equation corrects only this second step?
explanationMd: Starting from the correctly distributed equation, subtract 3x from both sides to obtain 7x−15=20. Add 15 to both sides to obtain 7x=35. The student subtracted 15 from the right side instead of adding it. Checking the resulting solution x=5 in the original equation gives 35 on both sides.

distractorRationale.d: This reverses the sign of the entire constant total after moving the negative fifteen.
distractorRationale.c: This adds the variable coefficients instead of subtracting the same 3x from both sides.
distractorRationale.b: This removes the negative fifteen from the left without applying the same operation on the right.
